newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian banks join Russian Eurobond syndicate.
newsitem.headline: Russian banks join Russian Eurobond syndicate.

text.p: Russia's 13th biggest bank by assets, Natsionalny Rezervny Bank, said it had joined a consortium set up by JP Morgan and SBC Warburg to help place Russia's planned Eurobond, an NRB official said on Wednesday.

Deputy Treasury head Andrei Serebryakov told Reuters JP Morgan and SBC Warburg will lead the consortium of some 20 Russian and Western banks, including CS First Boston, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, ABN-Amro, Dresdner Bank, NRB, and Russia's AKB Mezhdunarodnaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (MFK).
But NRB chairman Alexander Lebedev said NRB did not intend to market its allocation of Eurobonds, and would keep them for itself.
Russia's debut Eurobond is to be launched later this month.
The consortium is split into main and secondary distributor groups where NRB and MFK are in the secondary group, Serebryakov said.
Lebedev said he expected the secondary group to receive not more than one or two percent of the issue, which will total about $500 million.
"We counted for a more significant role, because as far as we know our quota will be very small," he said.
He said NRB would profit from a price rise in other Russian debt in its portfolio, as prices on older debt instruments move in line with the Eurobond terms.
"I think Russia can very well count on a tight spread over U.S. Treasuries," Lebedev said.
